title: Prompt Text Rule Checker
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims
Image Overlays
Prompt Writing
Text-Free Image Rule
Generative AI
description: A p5.js MicroSim in which learners judge each line of a shuffled draft image prompt as safe for a callout overlay or likely to put text into the image, get a one-sentence explanation for every line, and see a safe rewrite for each risky line.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: The text-free image rule for overlay image prompts
learningObjectives: The learner will judge whether a line of an image prompt is safe for a callout overlay or violates the text-free image rule, and will justify the judgment.
prerequisites: The text-free image rule and overlay image prompt template (Chapter 10)
Callout labels and the overlay data file (Chapter 10)

accessibility.notes: describe() is updated with the selected line and score; judged rows show a check or cross and the word safe or risky, not color alone; all buttons are native controls

dataFiles: Pool of 16 prompt lines (8 safe, 8 risky) with explanations and rewrites, embedded in prompt-text-rule-checker.js

controls.label: Prompt line
controls.purpose: Select a line of the draft prompt

controls.label: Keeps image text-free
controls.purpose: Judge the selected line as safe

controls.label: Risks text in image
controls.purpose: Judge the selected line as risky

controls.label: Show rewrite
controls.purpose: Show a safe replacement for a judged risky line

controls.label: New prompt
controls.purpose: Draw and shuffle a new draft of 10 (or 8) lines

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge-then-explain with immediate feedback and worked rewrites
keyQuestions: Which words in a prompt line invite the model to draw text or marks?
Why is a line that mentions text sometimes safe?
How can a risky line be rewritten to keep its visual intent?
commonMisconceptions: Any line containing numbers is risky (file dimensions are safe)
Only explicit requests for labels are risky (a labeled-diagram style also invites text)
Arrows and numbered circles are not text (they duplicate the engine's markers and leader lines)
assessmentOpportunities: Score of correct judgments out of attempts
Learner-written reasons and rewrites compared with the given ones
